Core Capabilities

Give every conclusion a clear line of support

The goal is not to accumulate information. It is to help a decision owner see the recommendation, its basis, its conditions, and the next move.

01 · FRAME

Frame the decision first

Set the audience, decision owner, options, evaluation criteria, time horizon, and hard constraints.

02 · TRACE

Trace evidence at claim level

Assign stable IDs to sources, supplied material, calculations, and assumptions, then cite what supports each claim.

03 · LABEL

Keep uncertainty visible

Separate facts, inferences, assumptions, and recommendations. Preserve conditions, timing, and limitations.

04 · ARGUE

Match the storyline to the choice

Use decision-first, options comparison, SCQA, or evidence synthesis with takeaway headlines that move the argument forward.

05 · CONTRACT

Work from one content contract

Keep slide content, evidence, visual type, limitations, and speaker notes in structured form.

06 · DELIVER

Deliver an offline-ready deck

Produce self-contained HTML and ship the structured content and source manifest with it.

How It Works

Fix the decision boundary before content and visual production begin

STEP 01

Frame the decision

Define who decides, what must be chosen, which options are in scope, and which constraints cannot move.

STEP 02

Collect and register evidence

Read supplied material; research externally only when authorized, prioritizing primary sources for consequential claims.

STEP 03

Choose the argument structure

Match the storyline to the decision instead of forcing a fixed slide count or generic section template.

STEP 04

Write the content contract

Specify each slide's takeaway, claims, visuals, limitations, and evidence relationships.

STEP 05

Generate the presentation

Create the offline HTML deck and source package in one delivery flow; produce a PDF only when requested.

STEP 06

Review the reading experience

Read every page at desktop and mobile widths, checking content, charts, sources, and navigation.

Case Studies

Three real decisions, one consistent evidence discipline

The examples span a team activity, a task-management platform, and a meeting cadence—covering options comparison, product selection, and operating-process change.

Options comparison

A half-day activity for a 12-person Shanghai team

Compare indoor interaction, a city-park activity, and a craft workshop within RMB 4,000, four hours, and a low-weather-risk preference.

RecommendationPrioritize indoor interaction at a conditional budget of about RMB 2,256; retain the craft workshop as backup.

Use the park only if conditions are stable 72 hours before the event; confirm capacity and final pricing before booking.

Tool selection

Task management for an eight-person content team

Compare Trello, Asana, and Notion across cost, adoption, project management, collaboration, and automation.

RecommendationChoose Trello Standard, subject to a two-week pilot using one real editorial workflow.

Move to Asana Starter if complex dependencies, Gantt views, or cross-project reporting become requirements.

Process change

Stand-up cadence for a 10-person team

Assess whether to replace a daily 30-minute stand-up with three weekly syncs and asynchronous updates on the remaining workdays.

RecommendationMeasure one baseline week, then run a four-week pilot with three sync days and two async days.

Use transparency, on-time updates, and blocker response as continuation guardrails; do not assume productivity will improve.

Reliability

Sources, calculations, and limitations stay with the deliverable

Primary sources for consequential claims

Prefer official pricing and product documentation, government material, peer-reviewed papers, and recognized research institutions.

Reproducible calculations

Record input evidence, formulas, units, periods, and display precision, then use the same results in charts.

Limitations remain visible

Keep pricing conditions, unconfirmed capacity, measures still to collect, and management assumptions in view.

No live webpage dependency

The deck contains the styles, scripts, and graphics it needs for meetings, internal sharing, and archiving.

Target Users

Built for teams expected to deliver the conclusion, evidence, and conditions together

Team leads

Understand the options, trade-offs, and next move quickly.

Operations and project managers

Compare alternatives, quantify constraints, and form an executable recommendation.

Strategy and research teams

Organize multiple sources into a reviewable argument without erasing uncertainty.

Client advisory and executive reporting teams

Present the recommendation, supporting evidence, and decision conditions in one delivery.
